input.question: How is Titan able to have an atmosphere pressure similar to Earth when it's gravity is so much lower than Earth's?
input.ground_truth: Cold makes sticky. Titan can hang on to so much atmosphere even though it’s gravity is much weaker, because the cold temperature means the collisions of gas particles are less energetic. Thus less likely to bounce hard enough that Titans gravity can’t recollect them.

Now, about the air (atmosphere):

Also, Titan is very cold, and cold air likes to stick close to the ground. Plus, Titan’s air is made of different stuff—mostly nitrogen, just like most of Earth’s air. Because Titan is far from the Sun and doesn’t lose its air as quickly as some other places, it keeps its thick blanket of air.

So even though Titan’s gravity is weak, it still has a lot of air, and that means the “squeeze” or pressure of the air is kind of similar to what we have on Earth! But it’s a little different, and you’d still need a special suit to breathe there.
